requirements.text: Build the app with Vite + React + TypeScript and use react-router for routing.
Use plain CSS with a design-token theme defined as CSS custom properties.
Running `npm run build` produces dist/index.html.
The site is static, with no backend and no user accounts.
No analytics and no third-party scripts are included.
No external font CDNs or image CDNs are used; only system font stacks are used.
The brand name shown is "The Bayes Group" and the tagline is "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business."
The colour palette is deep navy (#0B1F3A) and white with a single accent colour, teal #1F8A8A, defined as theme tokens.
The site has generous whitespace and looks like a top-tier professional consulting firm.
Headings use a serif system font stack.
Body text uses a clean sans-serif system font stack.
The wordmark logo is inline SVG: a small bell-curve mark followed by the text "The Bayes Group".
The layout works on a 390px wide phone viewport without horizontal scrolling.
The layout works on a 1440px wide desktop viewport without horizontal scrolling.
On phones, the header navigation collapses into a "Menu" button.
Activating the "Menu" button opens the navigation links.
Activating the "Menu" button again closes the navigation links.
Every page has the same header containing the wordmark, which links to /.
The header contains the nav links Services, Training, About and Contact.
The header contains a "Book a consultation" button linking to /contact.
Every page has the same footer containing the wordmark.
The footer contains the line "AI enablement, training and custom development."
The footer contains the nav links Services, Training, About and Contact.
The footer contains "© 2026 The Bayes Group".
The home page sets the document title "The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI".
The Services page sets the document title "Services | The Bayes Group".
The Training page sets a document title in the "<Page> | The Bayes Group" format (e.g. "Training | The Bayes Group").
The About page sets a document title in the "<Page> | The Bayes Group" format (e.g. "About | The Bayes Group").
The Contact page sets a document title in the "<Page> | The Bayes Group" format.
The Page not found page sets a document title in the "<Page> | The Bayes Group" format.
Every page has exactly one h1.
The home page (/) hero has the h1 "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business."
The home hero shows one sentence of value proposition.
The home hero has a "Book a consultation" button linking to /contact.
The home hero has an "Explore services" button linking to /services.
The home page has an "AI Enablement" pillar card with two or three sentences and a "Learn more" link to /services#enablement.
The home page has a "Training" pillar card with two or three sentences and a "Learn more" link to /services#training.
The home page has a "Custom Development" pillar card with two or three sentences and a "Learn more" link to /services#custom-development.
The home page has a "How we work" section with four numbered steps in order: Assess, Design, Build, Enable, each with one sentence.
The home page has a "Why The Bayes Group" section with a point about credentialed data scientists.
The "Why The Bayes Group" section has a point about hands-on builders.
The "Why The Bayes Group" section has a point about vendor-neutral advice.
The "Why The Bayes Group" section has a point about knowledge transfer so your team owns the result.
The home page ends with a call-to-action band reading "Ready to put AI to work?" with a "Book a consultation" button.
The home page sections appear in order: hero, pillar cards, How we work, Why The Bayes Group, call-to-action band.
The Services page (/services) has the h1 "Services".
The Services page has sections with ids enablement, training and custom-development, in that order.
The enablement section lists "AI readiness assessment" with a one-sentence description.
The enablement section lists "use-case discovery and prioritization" with a one-sentence description.
The enablement section lists "AI strategy and roadmap" with a one-sentence description.
The enablement section lists "AI governance and responsible-AI policy" with a one-sentence description.
The training section lists "executive AI briefings" with a one-sentence description.
The training section lists "hands-on team workshops" with a one-sentence description.
The training section lists "deep-learning bootcamps for technical teams" with a one-sentence description.
The training section lists "custom curricula" with a one-sentence description.
The custom-development section lists "LLM and retrieval-augmented (RAG) applications" with a one-sentence description.
The custom-development section lists "AI agents and workflow automation" with a one-sentence description.
The custom-development section lists "predictive models and ML pipelines" with a one-sentence description.
The custom-development section lists "deep-learning solutions" with a one-sentence description.
The custom-development section lists "integration with existing systems" with a one-sentence description.
The enablement section ends with a "Typical engagement" line (e.g. "2 to 6 weeks").
The training section ends with a "Typical engagement" line.
The custom-development section ends with a "Typical engagement" line.
The Training page (/training) has the h1 "Training".
The Training page shows a catalog of at least six course cards.
Each course card shows the course title.
Each course card shows its audience, which is exactly one of: Executives, Managers, Technical teams.
Each course card shows its format, which is one of: Half-day briefing, 1-day workshop, Multi-week bootcamp.
Each course card shows its duration.
Each course card shows a "You will learn" list of exactly three items.
At least one course exists for the Executives audience.
At least one course exists for the Managers audience.
At least one course exists for the Technical teams audience.
Four filter buttons appear above the catalog: All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams.
"All" is selected initially and shows every course.
Choosing "Executives" shows only Executives courses.
Choosing "Managers" shows only Managers courses.
Choosing "Technical teams" shows only Technical teams courses.
Choosing "All" after another filter shows every course again.
The selected filter button has aria-pressed="true" and the other filter buttons do not.
The selected filter button is visibly marked.
The About page (/about) has the h1 "About".
The About page has a mission paragraph.
The About page has a "Why Bayes" paragraph explaining that Bayesian reasoning, updating beliefs as evidence arrives, is how the firm approaches every engagement.
The About page has two founder cards, each with name "Founder Name" and role "Co-founder & Principal Data Scientist".
Each founder card has a credentials list clearly marked as a placeholder to be replaced.
Each founder card has a short bio clearly marked as a placeholder to be replaced.
The About page lists the value "Evidence over hype".
The About page lists the value "Build to transfer".
The About page lists the value "Vendor-neutral".
The About page lists the value "Responsible by design".
The Contact page (/contact) has the h1 "Book a consultation".
The Contact page shows the email hello@thebayesgroup.com.
The contact form has a labelled Name field.
The contact form has a labelled Email field.
The contact form has a labelled Company field.
The contact form has a labelled select "What can we help with?" with options AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Not sure yet.
The contact form has a labelled Message field.
The contact form has a "Send message" submit button.
Submitting with an empty Name shows "Please enter your name." next to the Name field.
Submitting with an empty Email shows "Please enter a valid email address." next to the Email field.
Submitting with an invalidly formatted Email shows "Please enter a valid email address." next to the Email field.
Submitting with an empty Message shows "Please enter a message." next to the Message field.
On submit, each invalid field shows its own error at the same time, and valid fields show no error.
An invalid submit sends nothing and shows no success message.
A valid submit makes no network request.
A valid submit shows "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day."
A valid submit clears the form fields.
Any unknown route shows a page with the h1 "Page not found".
The Page not found page has a link back to the home page (/).
Pages use the semantic landmarks header, nav, main and footer.
Every form field has an associated label.
Keyboard focus is visible on interactive elements.
Text colours meet WCAG AA contrast against their backgrounds.
